title.rendered: Forgive Us As We Forgive, Deliver Us From Evil | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 5

excerpt.rendered: A servant forgiven ten thousand talents walked out and seized a fellow servant by the throat over a hundred denarii. That parable is Jesus’ commentary on the next two petitions of the prayer.

content.rendered:
Jesus told the story of a servant who had been forgiven a debt of ten thousand talents, then walked out and seized a fellow servant by the throat over a debt of a hundred denarii. The story was Jesus’ commentary on the next two petitions of the prayer He had just taught His disciples. Forgive us as we forgive. Deliver us from evil.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, October 7, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 5

Today’s Scripture

“And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.”
Matthew 6:12-13 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In Matthew 18, Jesus told the parable of a servant who owed his king ten thousand talents, an impossibly vast sum, roughly equal to the entire annual revenue of a Roman province. The king called the servant in to settle the account. The servant could not pay. The king, moved with compassion, cancelled the entire debt. Forgiven. Wiped clean. Released. The servant walked out of the king’s presence a free man. Then he met a fellow servant on the road who owed him a hundred denarii — about three months’ wages. He grabbed his fellow by the throat and demanded immediate payment. When the fellow could not pay, the forgiven servant had him thrown into prison. The other servants reported this back to the king. And the king, furious, called the first servant back in. “You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Should you not also have had compassion on your fellow servant, just as I had pity on you?”

That parable is Jesus’ commentary on the two petitions that close the heart of the Lord’s Prayer. “Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.” These two petitions go together because they are the same posture in two directions. Forgiveness received flows into forgiveness given. The believer who refuses to forgive the small debt owed by a neighbour has misunderstood the enormous debt the Father has already cancelled at the cross. And a believer who harbours unforgiveness opens the door to the evil one, who uses unresolved bitterness as his primary foothold in the believer’s life. The two petitions, prayed together, close the door the enemy would otherwise walk through.

The Passion Translation renders these petitions with striking depth: “Forgive us the wrongs we have done as we ourselves release forgiveness to those who have wronged us. Rescue us every time we face tribulations and set us free from evil” (Matthew 6:12-13 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven (left, remitted, and let go of the debts, and have given up resentment against) our debtors. And lead (bring) us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one” (Matthew 6:12-13 AMPC). Let go of the debts. Give up resentment. The believer’s forgiveness of others is active, decisive, and complete.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Two petitions, linked. The believer asks for forgiveness in the same breath as the believer extends forgiveness. The format trains the heart. You cannot pray this petition sincerely while harbouring active unforgiveness toward another person.

The Essence. The believer prays from the finished work of the cross, not toward it. The debt was cancelled at Calvary. The believer’s forgiveness is already secured. The petition is not a request to be forgiven, as if forgiveness were still uncertain. It is a renewal of the believer’s walk in the forgiveness already granted, and a corresponding release of others.

The Authority. The believer has authority to forgive sins committed against them. Jesus made this explicit after His resurrection: “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them” (John 20:23). This is Kingdom authority. The believer wields the keys of forgiveness in the earth, releasing people from the debts they owe personally, so that the enemy cannot use those unresolved debts as a weapon against the believer’s own walk.

The Assurance. 1 John 1:9 declares: “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” There is no uncertainty. The believer who comes to the Father in confession walks out of the presence cleansed, every time. The assurance is in His faithfulness, not in the believer’s performance.

The Submission. This petition submits the believer’s natural desire for retribution to the Father’s authority. The believer who prays “forgive me as I forgive” is explicitly surrendering the right to hold grudges, nurse offences, or seek revenge. Vengeance belongs to the Father, not to the believer.

The Result. A clean heart, a closed door to the enemy, and a believer walking in freedom and spiritual authority. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, is there a debt someone owes you that you have been holding onto? A hurt. A betrayal. An unpaid loan. A broken promise. The ten thousand talents the Father has already cancelled for you is infinitely greater than the hundred denarii being held against your name. Release the debt. Walk free. Deny the enemy the foothold he has been using. Pray this petition today with the whole of your heart.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done. Give us this day our daily bread.

Forgiveness Received. Father, I receive again today the complete forgiveness You have granted me at the cross. My debt was ten thousand talents. You cancelled it. I walk out of Your presence as a forgiven son/daughter.

Forgiveness Released. And in the authority of the forgiveness I have received, I release [name the person who has wronged you]. I let go of the debt. I give up the resentment. I close the door the enemy has been using. The account is cleared.

Deliverance. Deliver me from the evil one. Keep me from temptation. Protect me today in the places where I am weak. In Jesus’ name, I resist the devil and he flees.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am completely forgiven at the cross. I walk in that forgiveness, and I release every debt owed to me by anyone, in the same measure. The enemy has no foothold in my life. I am delivered from evil, in Jesus’ name.
